title: NEO: Saving GPU Memory Crisis with CPU Offloading for Online LLM Inference
technique: offload part of decode attention and KV cache to host CPU; asymmetric GPU-CPU pipelining and load-aware scheduling

optimized_metrics.evidence: This paper aims to achieve higher throughput for online LLM inference without compromising accuracy or latency
This paper aims to achieve higher throughput for online LLM inference without compromising accuracy or latency
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: For each request, we compute its per-token latency by dividing its full latency by its output token number, and then we take the average among all requests.

headline_claim.text: N EO achieves up to 7.5x, 26%, and 14% higher throughput compared to GPU-only approach on T4, A10G, and H100 GPUs, respectively, while maintaining the same latency

metric_definitions.definition_quote: For each request, we compute its per-token latency by dividing its full latency by its output token number, and then we take the average among all requests.
metric_definitions.notes: This is normalized latency (E2E/output tokens), not TPOT/TBT.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: the GPU token throughput, i.e., the total time elapsed divided by the total number of tokens processed (input length + output length)
metric_definitions.notes: As written the ratio is inverted (time/tokens); counts input+output tokens.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: 14.3% higher throughput on H100 (at 2 sec latency), 6.40% higher on A10G (at 2 sec latency), and 563% higher on T4 (at 1 sec latency)
metric_definitions.notes: Throughput read off the load-latency curve at a fixed average per-token latency, i.e. latency-bounded throughput (units not stated; request rate).

slo_spec: no SLO; latency-bounded throughput read at average per-token latency of 1-2 s
load_regime: Poisson request-rate sweep (load-latency curves); offline fixed workloads
tradeoff_acknowledged: KV offload could raise latency at high rates: 'NEO's latency gets slightly higher' as request rate grows vs heavily optimized vLLM
hardware: T4, A10G, H100 + host CPU (AWS g5)
workloads: Azure LLM coding trace; OpenAI summarization comparison; synthetic
extractor_notes: Scheduler's per-iteration goal is stated as 'maximize T/x' (iteration time over batch size, sic) and picks the schedule with higher estimated throughput. Only mean per-token latency curve; Fig 7 shows full distribution but no tail target.
load_class_quote: "We evaluate the online latency of NEO under various request rates. We sample request arrival timestamps following the Poisson process." (§5.2); offline throughput also reported (Fig 7b) but headline is throughput at same latency under load
